{
  "hook": "High-altitude Garnacha from the Sierra de Gredos demands attention for its purity of fruit and granite-driven minerality. El Reventón pulls from century-old vines rooted in sandy granite soils, delivering a transparency rarely seen at this price point.",
  "wine_summary": "Daniel Landi and Fernando García revived this forgotten corner of Castilla y León by focusing on single-vineyard expressions rather than bulk production. Their work in Cebreros proves that Garnacha thrives on poor, acidic granite soils when farmed biodynamically. This bottle represents the entry point into their hierarchy, yet it retains the structural integrity of their top crus.",
  "terroir_expression": "At 800 to 1,200 meters above sea level, the Sierra de Gredos creates a continental climate with sharp thermal shifts that preserve acidity in the grapes. Decomposed granite slopes provide excellent drainage, forcing vines to dig deep for water and nutrients. These conditions yield thinner skins and lower yields, translating to a wine with bright red fruit and a stony, saline finish rather than jammy density.",
  "vinification_summary": "Using native yeasts allows spontaneous conversion of sugars, which often adds complexity to the aroma profile. The wine sees 14 months in oak, softening the tannins without masking the primary fruit character. Whole clusters during fermentation introduce stem tannins, adding structure and a herbal lift to the mid-palate.",
  "food_pairing": "Pair with roasted lamb shoulder with rosemary to cut through the wine's acidity while matching its savory depth. Grilled octopus with paprika works because the smoky char complements the granite minerality. For a casual option, try mushroom pizza with mozzarella; the earthiness mirrors the wine's forest floor notes.",
  "comparable_wines": "Priorat offers similar intensity but with more density due to different soils. Domaine Gramenon Côtes du Rhône provides a similar biodynamic philosophy and fresh Garnacha profile.",
  "style_profile": "Medium-bodied dry red with bright acidity and granite-driven structure",
  "cellar_recommendation": "This wine survives storage in a cool, dark place away from vibration for up to a decade. Decant for one hour before serving to allow the aromas to open up.",
  "value_assessment": "$65 to $85 places this above standard Crianza but below top-tier Priorat collectors' items. Competitors like Álvaro Palacios Camins del Priorat offer similar quality at a slightly lower cost. The biodynamic certification and vine age justify the premium for buyers seeking transparency.",
  "market_position": "On restaurant lists, sommeliers feature this label targeting diners who want Old World structure without heavy oak influence. Serious collectors seek this label for its consistency across vintages in a warming climate.",
  "insider_take": "Warning for buyers who prefer ripe, high-alcohol styles from hotter regions because the acidity here is prominent. The 2021 vintage offers better balance than the warmer 2022, providing more freshness for immediate drinking.",
  "aging_potential_years": 15,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 2,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 12,
  "sensory": {
